key_insight: Learning a self-supervised prior over frame-to-frame latent motion extracted from the same unlabeled videos used to train generators can strongly improve physical and motion consistency in video diffusion models without relying on simulators or curated physics data.
problem_solved: Modern video generators produce realistic frames but often fail to maintain physically plausible, temporally consistent motion across frames; this work addresses motion realism and physical consistency in generated video.
method: Extract frame-to-frame motion cues in latent space from unlabeled videos and train a motion prior self-supervisedly.
Formulate the prior as a latent motion model that regularizes or conditions the video diffusion/generation process to favor physically consistent transitions.
Integrate the learned latent motion prior into training/sampling to reduce unrealistic dynamics without external simulators or teacher models.
impact: Provides a scalable, data-efficient way to improve motion realism in video generation, making generative models more reliable for simulation, planning, and downstream tasks that require physically consistent dynamics.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: video frames → encoder to latents → compute frame-to-frame latent deltas → learn latent motion prior → condition video generator
Before/after video frame sequences comparing standard diffusion outputs vs. outputs conditioned on LaMo (highlighting improved motion continuity)
Schematic of latent space trajectories showing smoothed/physically coherent transitions enforced by the motion prior
Bar chart or table summarizing quantitative improvements (e.g., motion-consistency metrics) and qualitative examples
paper_title: LaMo: Self-Supervised Latent Motion Priors for Physical Realism in Video Generation
paper_authors: Bo Jiang, Depu Meng, Yihan Hu, Yichen Xie, Tianshuo Xu
